 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 08-04-2021 at about 9.00 p.m., while petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-EB-4998 to go to Manjunatha.B.R vs Suhil Ahamad on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103681222/
2 KSRTC Bus Stop at Kanaka Circle, when he reached Opp.
Basaveswara Hospital, K.M.Road, Kadur Town, at that time a Bollero Pickup Bearing No.KA-24-8741 came from Opposite side with high speed in rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed against his motor cycle.

entities.text: KSRTC Bus Stop at Kanaka Circle
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Kadur, wherein he took first aid and then shifted to Shivamogga Govt. Hospital and then shifted to Digvijaya Hospital,
Banashankari, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for about 12 days,
surgery was conducted, rod was inserted, X-rays were done and advised to take followup treatment.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.6,00,000/- towards conveyance, food nourishment, medical and attendant charges.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident he was working as bakery cake maker in Maruthi Bakery Kadur and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accident he lost his income and future prospects and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to this accident he has lost the income and future prospective life, happiness and earning capacity and has become disabled and dependant.
4. The Kadur Police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA- 24-8741 in Cr.No.80/2021 under Section 279 & 337 of IPC R/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
The accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 1 st respondent.
The policy was valid and was in force at the time of accident.
The driver of the said Bollero vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents.
5. After service of summons, both the respondents appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 has not chosen to file the written statement.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the averments made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741 as on the date of alleged accident.
It has not issued any policy for the said vehicle covering the date of accident.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the petition against this respondent is liable to be dismissed.
It is further contended that if the claimant has furnished any policy particulars then this respondent may be permitted to file additional written statement.
The person driving the vehicle has "no relation in force" as on the date of accident to drive the vehicle.
The driver of the vehicle has not valid and effective driving license to drive the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-24-8741 at the time of accident.

It has further contended that the owner of the vehicle knowingly allowed the driver to drive the said vehicle without valid and effective driving license and there is violation of the policy conditions by the owner of the insured vehicle.
The insured vehicle was not having FC to ply the vehicle in a place of Manjunatha.

3 accident i.e., public placed and the same was used without having valid permit in violation of the policy condition and also the MV Act.
This respondent seeks protection under Sec. 147, 149 and also under sec.134 of MV Act.

It is the mandatory duty of the owner of the vehicle to furnish the particulars of the policy, date, time and place of accident, particulars of injured and the name of the driver etc., but the owner of the vehicle has filed to comply with the statutory demand.

As per Sec.158 (6) of M.V Act 1988 it is the mandatory duty of the concerned PS to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of information but the Kadur Police have failed to forward the documents and complied with the statutory demand.
The petitioner was not wearing safety head gear at the time of accident and hence there is violation of breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
It has denied the injuries sustained and amount spent towards the medical expenses.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exaggerated one.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned Predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, 08- 04-2021 at about 9.00 a.m., he was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing No.KA- 18-EB-4998 towards Kanaka Circle and when he reached Opp. Basaveshwara Hospital, K.M.Road, Kadur Town,
at that time Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA-24- 8741 being driven by its driver at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed his motor cycle, as a result, he fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner in order to prove his case he himself has examined as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13.
Dr.Nagaraj.
B.N is examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.P.14 & 15 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced their rebuttal evidence and respondent evidence is taken as Nil.
8. The case is posted for arguments, at this stage, Unfortunately, the petitioner expired on 29-04-2024 i.e., during the pendency of the petition.
Hence his Legal representative was brought on record as petitioner vide orders dated 27-02-2025.

9. Heard the arguments from counsel for petitioner. Perused the entire materials placed on record.
10.

My answers to the above points are as follows :-

REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
In order to prove the actionable negligence, petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.

He has filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and has re- iterated the averments made in the petition and has produced FIR, Complaint, Spot panchanama, sketch map, Seizure Mahazar,
IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet as Ex.P.1 to 7, by these oral and documentary evidence Petitioner proved that, there was an accident in which he sustained injury.

12. On perusal of complaint Ex.P.1 which reveals that petitioner has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the complaint, Kadur Police have registered FIR against the driver of Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741 .
13. With regard to negligence, Respondent No.2 has mainly contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
Except this suggestion, Respondents have not produced any material to show the non-involvement and negligence of the petitioner.
14. Moreover, neither the owner nor the driver of the offending Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741 has challenged the charge sheet.
The I.O has filed charge sheet after completion of investigation based on the evidences available at the spot.
15. All the records indicate the negligence of driver of the offending Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741 .
Respondents have also failed to prove the allegations of the petitioner with regard to the injury sustained by her in the alleged accident.

By the above materials and evidences it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in RTA due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.2:-
During pendency of the petition, the petitioner cum injured - Sri.Manjunath.B.R died and his legal representatives were brought on record.

The main contention of the second respondent that, as per medical records like wound certificate it is very clear that the injuries sustained by petitioner is simple in nature and there is no grievous injuries and there is no nexus between injuries and death.

Moreover, the Postmortem examination of the deceased has not been conducted to find out the cause of his death and no evidence is place on record to prove that the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in the accident.

17. In the absence of such proof, as per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2010 KAR MAC 557 between Somavva & others V/s Vijaya Kumar and others, the legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to claim only expenses spent towards the treatment of the deceased petitioner and the loss of income suffered by the deceased during laid-up/treatment period.

It is well settled law that when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken in to consideration as notional income.
The next question is how to consider the notional income in the eye of law.
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 15.11.2021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased petitioner.

19. As per the medical records the original petitioner has sustained grievous injury to the Petitioner had sustained- Left distal clavicle fracture malunited shaft clavicle left distal radius fracture, left frontal depressed fracture EDH.
The above mentioned injuries are grievous injuries in nature and he took treatment at Govt. Hospital, Kadur to the said accidental injuries.
and to the all over body and still he was under the medical treatment.
It is needless to say that the above injuries are grievous in nature.

The as per Ex.P.8 - discharge summary issued by Digvijaya Hospital, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 09-04- 2021 to 17-04-2021 i.e., 9 days.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

PW.1 has produced Ex.P.9 medical bills total amount of Rs.4,83,221/-
towards medical expenses and also produced 21 medical prescriptions.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the bills.
Though respondent No.2 counsel had cross examined PW.1 at length but nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the version of PW.1.

Hence an amount of Rs.4,83,221/- is awarded under this head and attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, as already stated supra the deceased petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 9 days as it could be seen from Ex.P. 8, therefore, this tribunal inclines to award Rs.13,500/- under this head.
21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD: The period of hospitalization of 9 days is proved.
Considering the nature of injuries and treatment given, it is quite natural that the deceased could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.45,000/- (15,000 X 3) under this head.

22. The calculation table stands as follows:
 Sl. Compensation head Amount  No.
 2 Loss of income during 45,000/-
 laid-up period  3 Attendant charges, extra 13,500/-
 nutritious food &
 conveyance charges  4 Medical expenses 4,83,221/-
 TOTAL Rs.5,41,721/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,41,721/-.

6 23.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
The petitioners being the Legal representative of the deceased (Sri.Manjunath.B.R) is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,41,221/-.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer and

respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Bollerro Pickup vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-24/8741 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the Legal Representative of the deceased petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.3

: In view of the findings given on issues No.1 and 2 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:

The Legal Representatives of deceased petitioner is entitled to get compensation of Rs.5,41,721/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Forty One Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty One)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 80% Petitioner No.2 and 3 - 5% each Petitioner No.4 and 5 - 5%
each

After deposit, the entire compensation amount of apportionment together with interest shall be released to the LR's of deceased petitioner, i.e petitioner No. 1 and 4 and 5 through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

Since the petitioner No.2 and 3 are minor, the entire apportionment amount of Petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be deposited in their name as FD in any nationalized /scheduled bank till he attains the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
